sections.name: Radscorpions
sections.card:
Summary: Big armored scorpions of the Mojave that run straight at you in packs of two to five, striking with claws and a poisoned tail. They are rough on a low-level Courier, and Damage Threshold means an unprepared Courier struggles to put them down.
Weak points: The claws are the softest part, and crippling them stuns the scorpion. Armor-piercing weapons work well against it, with the Guns skill. Do not hope for a head shot bonus: it has no head or other spot that takes extra damage, which blunts V.A.T.S. and ordinary firearms.
Looks like: Apart from size, an ordinary scorpion with a mottled, dark blue-gray shell. The common kind runs from a large dog to small livestock in size, and the rare queen is bigger than a Corvega.
Tips: The giant radscorpion is rarer and faster, hits much harder and has a Damage Threshold like a sentry bot's, and some stand just outside Goodsprings and its cemetery, so you can meet one very early. Only two queens are known: one is south of the Nipton Road pit stop, in the scorpion burrow, and the other is in the Searchlight fire station, reached during a side quest. Ruby Nash will cook you a casserole if you bring her a radscorpion gland.

sections.name: Geckos
sections.card:
Summary: Reptile packs found across the whole Mojave. When one gecko fights, the whole pack joins in, charging or leaping in with open jaws and clawing quickly. Some kinds breathe fire or spit poison from a distance.
Looks like: A lizard with two fins sprouting behind the head, orange-tinted eyes and five fingers and toes, anywhere from a small child's size to taller than a grown adult. Golden geckos have bright gold scales; fire geckos are mottled purple and red with spikes down the back.
Tips: Plain geckos, the mildest kind, roam around Goodsprings and near the Mojave Outpost, and along Interstate 15 toward Primm. Golden geckos live in irradiated places such as Crescent Canyon, Vault 34 and Cottonwood crater, and their attacks do heavy radiation damage. Fire geckos favor mountains and caves such as Lucky Jim Mine and Nopah Cave. The Animal Friend perk works on geckos and golden geckos but not on fire geckos, which run if hit by a flare gun. Tanned gecko hides can be made into armor.

sections.name: Giant mantises
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated praying mantises that came out of Vault 22 and spread across the Mojave. Each is much smaller than a person, so they swarm whenever they can and mostly leap in to slice with their forelegs.
Weak points: Crippling a mantis's antennae sends it into a frenzy, so it lashes out at anything within reach.
Looks like: Much like a real praying mantis, only far bigger, though still smaller than a person. The young nymphs are tiny, and some die just from being walked over. The Zion Canyon kinds are larger.
Tips: Weak nymphs turn up early in the Goodsprings schoolhouse and Nevada Highway Patrol station; the adults wait later, around Spring Mt. Ranch State Park and on the road toward Jacobstown. Shooting an ootheca releases about a dozen nymphs, which then attack. Dead mantises can yield eggs and forelegs.

sections.name: Super mutants and nightkin
sections.card:
Summary: Tough armored mutants that favor heavy guns, plus melee weapons like the super sledge. Gunners walk slowly toward you while firing; melee fighters throw frag grenades and then rush in. Plain mutants give way to brutes and masters as you level.
Looks like: Brutes can be told apart by helmets and rough metal armor. Nightkin have deep purplish-blue skin and wear no armor.
Tips: Ordinary super mutants are armored to Damage Threshold 15, the same as combat armor; nightkin wear none but shrug off 30 percent of damage. Nightkin use Stealth Boys to creep up on their prey. Black Mountain is the main stronghold. Hostile ones reliably come back at Black Rock Cave, Jack Rabbit Springs and a small cave north of Ranger Station Bravo. The masters at Jacobstown are not hostile. Hostile ones often carry miniguns, light machine guns or super sledges that you can sell.

sections.name: Centaurs
sections.card:
Summary: Mutants that are somewhat humanoid in shape. They fire a slow, high-arcing radioactive spit and whip at close range with their tongues. One alone is no great danger, but they rarely come alone.
Weak points: They are slow and clumsy, and the spit travels so slowly that it is easy to sidestep.
Looks like: The common kind keeps only a human-like head and torso, with three long tentacle-like tongues where back spines would be. Evolved centaurs are bigger and more muscular, with thick clusters of tumors on their backs.
Tips: The tongue lash does little physical damage but a notable amount of radiation. Groups gather at Jack Rabbit Springs, south of Black Mountain, and in the Devil's Throat east of Bitter Springs, where evolved ones and the single giant evolved centaur stay. They respawn there three days after being killed.

sections.name: Bighorners
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated sheep, grazing wild in herds of three to seven or kept by settlements like Goodsprings and Jacobstown. They leave you alone until you or their young get close, then they bellow, charge and ram, and the entire herd joins in if one of them is upset.
Weak points: They are about as hardy as a radscorpion. A hit on the horns counts as a head shot, and a critical hit blows the head apart.
Looks like: A horned sheep; every bighorner grows horns, whatever its sex. Bulls are larger and stronger, and the young are about a third of full size.
Tips: The compass shows them hostile, but unprovoked ones do not chase you; leave them be and they graze. Their head-butts are brutal, flinging you back or knocking you down, and they run very fast; bulls in a group keep knocking you over. Hurting one of the young turns its relatives on you, and penned calves in towns are watched by ranchers who turn hostile if you harm them. With the Animal Friend perk they never turn on you.

sections.name: Giant ants
sections.card:
Summary: Large insects with big mandibles that can be a real nuisance early in the game. Workers wear you down with nonstop swarming attacks, and soldiers are the biggest of the usual kinds.
Weak points: A hit on the antennae counts as a critical hit and also sends the ant into a frenzy. A worker's shell is not especially hard next to a radscorpion's.
Looks like: A big ant in a yellow-brown shell with large mandibles and long antennae. The queen is the biggest creature anywhere in the Mojave.
Tips: They are not fast, so if you fight them from a distance you can simply walk away from them. Workers roam in groups across barren desert, including the Ivanpah race track and Ivanpah Dry Lake; several soldiers are inside the Allied Technologies offices. One queen exists, in the mound south of those offices. At the Nellis array the ants blow up if hit by energy weapons or explosives.

sections.name: Feral ghouls
sections.card:
Summary: Ghouls that lost their minds to heavy radiation exposure and attack everyone except their own kind. Shrill and fast, they are dangerous mainly in numbers or to a low-level Courier.
Weak points: A plain feral ghoul falls to one or two head shots from a decent ranged weapon, or one solid melee or unarmed hit.
Looks like: Like normal ghouls but with deformed faces, skinnier, and moving oddly. The plain kind wears only tattered shorts; reavers wear what look like scraps of metal armor.
Tips: Roamers are more dangerous than the plain kind and far more common. Reavers in the Mojave are no stronger than the other kinds and no longer give off radiation. Glowing ones turn up at higher levels where radiation is worst, with much more health and damage and a burst of radiation. Expect ferals in the Vegas sewers and around Hell's Motel, the Devil's Throat and the Nevada Highway Patrol station. The armor they wear is for show.

sections.name: Sentry bots
sections.card:
Summary: Heavy military robots on wheeled tripod legs, armed with a Gatling laser or minigun on one side and a missile launcher on the other. They have a lot of health, so they are hard to put down, especially at a low level.
Weak points: They are open to electromagnetic pulses, so pulse grenades, pulse mines and any other EMP-producing weapon can hurt them badly. Destroying the combat inhibitor mounted on its back sends it berserk, and it then attacks everything around it.
Looks like: Armored head, wheeled tripod base. The REPCONN ones are shorter, with green eyes instead of red and REPCONN in white across the chest.
Tips: At long range a sentry bot leans on its missiles; once you are close it switches to the minigun or Gatling laser to avoid splash on itself. Head shots do less damage to it. Hardened sentry bots, met with hardened Mister Gutsies near the crashed vertibird, have about 500 hit points against 300 but no armor at all, and resist pulse grenades better. Twelve REPCONN bots hide in the headquarters and come out if you trip the alarm.
